Georgetown

Shay Montgomery talks about Victor Tranh and how Georgetown was exposed to DC-62 Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1]

That's where Victor Tranh came in. Professor Tranh was a big deal in neighborhood politics, and it didn't take much for him to convince people that the right thing to do was evict the patients and spray the neighborhood. It would make all of them safe, he promised. Now I knew this was bullshit - they hadn't had any time to run tests on this DC-62 stuff he was talking about - and I said so. Loudly. And that's when Victor Tranh lied. He told people I was sick, too, which I wasn't, at least not yet. He had me kicked out with the rest of the infected. Sent us to the CERA camp down by the river and sprayed his DC-62. I hear it killed him. Justice, she works in funny ways. [1]

Making a Difference

Shay Montgomery talks about a family she helped after escaping the camps Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1]

I could tell that story about twenty different families around the city, and all those stories would be true. I'm not bragging. I'm asking you what you're doing to make a difference, and if you're just surviving, to think about doing a little more than that. [1]

Reflective

Shay Montgomery reflects on her life before the lockdown and how far she has come Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1]

I don't even know if anyone else who was at that party is still alive. And yet here I am, about to breach the Capital Station Dark Zone again, looking for meds for the people who've fallen through the cracks of whatever system's left. I like to think I'm doing the right thing. [1]

Capital Station

Shay Montgomery talks about the events that led to Capitol Station being abandoned Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1]

I'm more interested in what got left at the field hospital. There's still meds there, still sterile equipment and surgical supplies. Hell, there's even clean toilet paper. I've been in there three times and haven't come close to cleaning it out. I worry 'm getting predictable. But so far, it's been worth the risk. [1]
